One Piece.text: Holds the record for the highest initial print run of any book in Japan.
One Piece.evidence: It holds various publishing records, including the highest initial print run for any book in Japan.

Doraemon.text: The robot cat fears mice because robotic mice chewed off his ears, and he turned blue from sadness.
Doraemon.evidence: Although Doraemon is a cat robot, he has a fear of mice because of an incident where robotic mice chewed off his ears. Afterwards, Doraemon lost his original yellow color and turned blue from sadness.

Golgo 13.text: The oldest manga still in publication; it has carried on since its creator Takao Saito died in 2021.
Golgo 13.evidence: Golgo 13 is the oldest manga still in publication, and its tankōbon edition was certified by Guinness World Records as the highest number of volumes for a manga series. Before his death in 2021, Saito said that he wanted the manga to continue on without him; he had previously said that he was worried that the manga might be left unfinished. The Saito Production group of manga creators continue its publication with the assistance of the Big Comic's editorial department.

Dragon Ball.text: Helped push Weekly Shōnen Jump to its highest circulation, 6.53 million copies a week.
Dragon Ball.evidence: Its initial serialization in Weekly Shōnen Jump was partly responsible for the magazine reaching its highest circulation of 6.53 million weekly sales.

Naruto.text: Grew out of two earlier one-shot manga by Masashi Kishimoto, one of them also called Naruto.
Naruto.evidence: The series is based on two one-shot manga by Kishimoto: Karakuri (1995), which earned Kishimoto an honorable mention in Shueisha's monthly Hop Step Award the following year, and Naruto (1997).

Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba.text: Its anime film Mugen Train became the highest-grossing anime and Japanese film of all time.
Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba.evidence: Its anime television series adaptation, produced by Ufotable, aired a 26-episode first season from April to September 2019, with a sequel film, Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba – The Movie: Mugen Train, released in October 2020, which became the highest-grossing anime and Japanese film of all time.

Slam Dunk.text: Its creator was commended by the Japan Basketball Association for helping popularise basketball in Japan.
Slam Dunk.evidence: In 2010, Inoue received special commendations from the Japan Basketball Association for helping popularize basketball in Japan.

KochiKame: Tokyo Beat Cops.text: Ran continuously in Weekly Shōnen Jump for 40 years, from 1976 to 2016.
KochiKame: Tokyo Beat Cops.evidence: It was continuously serialized in Shueisha's shōnen manga magazine Weekly Shōnen Jump for 40 years, from September 1976 to September 2016.

Jujutsu Kaisen.text: A sequel to Gege Akutami's earlier series, which was retroactively retitled Jujutsu Kaisen 0.
Jujutsu Kaisen.evidence: Jujutsu Kaisen is a sequel to Akutami's previous work, Tokyo Metropolitan Curse Technical School, which was retroactively titled Jujutsu Kaisen 0 following the release of Jujutsu Kaisen.
